I’m a big-time pandal hopper. Durga Puja evenings are something I look forward to every year. ❤️

Today, I got ready and stepped out to visit Ahiritola, Kumartuli, Chorbagan, Chaltabagan and other nearby pandals.

After visiting just two pujas, it started raining. I took a cab back home. When we passed near Chorbagan’s main entrance, I saw police personnel and civic volunteers. The rain had kept the crowd relatively thin, and for a moment, I thought of going back.

But with the rain and the difficulty of finding a cab, I decided to return home.

And then I saw the news.

Completely shattered. Heartbroken. Unable to process what happened.

I keep thinking… if it hadn’t rained, would I have still been there? Would I have been standing among those people?

There are so many thoughts running through my mind. So many unanswered questions. A strange, unsettling void that’s difficult to explain.

We go out to celebrate Maa Durga, to seek blessings, to create memories with our loved ones. Nobody steps out expecting that a festive evening could turn into their last.

People getting injured is heartbreaking enough. Losing lives while visiting a Durga Puja pandal is simply too devastating to comprehend.

Life is frighteningly unpredictable. Sometimes, a little rain, a delayed cab, or a small decision to return home can change everything.

Tonight, my heart goes out to every family that has lost a loved one and to everyone affected by this tragedy.

May they find the strength to endure this unimaginable pain. 🙏

Some festive evenings leave us with memories. Others leave us questioning how fragile life really is.

Om Shanti. 🙏

So there are some 3000 pandals in the city. Covering all of them won't be possible or practical. If you want to do just the big and famous one, even that would be some 200 pandals and on Ashtami/Navami visiting just one of them can eat up 5-6 hours. 

So this needs planning. Divide the city geograpically. Fix your priorities. Maximize the usage of day hours when rush is relatively lesser. 

Here are few routes. 

First and foremost my top 2 routes for those visiting Kolkata just for experiencing Pujo. 

1. Old/North Kolkata Heritage Route: These are the OG pujos.

Bagbazar Sarbojanin → Ahiritola Sarbojanin → Kumartuli Park → Sovabazar Rajbari → Hatibagan Sarbojanin → Nalin Sarkar Street → Tala Prattoy.

2. Kasba to Jodhpur Park - My go-to stretch. This is one of the longest stretch you can cover in one day covering 15+ famous ones if you are ready to do 50000 steps in a day. 

Start at Bosepukur Sitala Mandir → Bosepukur Talbagan → Ekdalia Evergreen → Singhi Park  → Deshapriya Park → Tridhara Sammilani → Hindustan Park → Maddox Square →Mudiali → Jodhpur Park

Then there are routes to cover depending upon where you staying:

Salt Lake Cluster: These have relatively lesser rush and can be easily covered within a few hours (unless you get stuck in FD block one which is largest in scale)
FD Block → AK Block → BJ Block → BD Block (plus you visit any additional blocks on the route)

Behala Cluster: Would recommend to visit these during night. Behala Club → Behala Buroshibtala Janakalyan Sangha → Behala Natun Dal → Barisha Club → Barisha Sarbojanin

VIP Road Cluster: Telengabagan → Sreebhumi Sporting Club → Lake Town Association → Dum Dum Park Tarun Sangha → Bharat Chakra → Dum Dum Park Youth Association 

Alipore Cluster: Alipore Sarbojanin → Chetla Agrani → Badamtala Ashar Sangha → 66 Pally → Suruchi Sangha

Garia Cluster: Naktala Udayan Sangha → Naktala Pally Unnayan Samity → Garia Naba Durga → Pancha Durga → Patuli Sarbojanin 

If you are not from Kolkata, I would suggest avoid the big Pujas of Central Kolkata (Md. Ali Park → Santosh Mitra Square → College Square). They get insane crowd from people flocking Kolkata from nearby districts for a day due to nearness to Sealdah and Howrah stations. They are very popular but you need adventurous spirit to tackle them.
